title: DiLaDiff: Distilled Latent-augmented Diffusion for Language Modeling
claim: A learned continuous latent, generated by a distilled diffusion prior, conditions a discrete denoiser, so the two stages compose into one pipeline.
layout: 3 grouped modules, left-to-right, with iterative loop arrows and a dashed encoding bypass
description: A left-to-right block diagram with three zones. At far left, input x feeds a grey Encoder box E_phi(z|x). A dashed grey arrow labelled 'Encoding' arcs over the top to the latent z. The center zone is a light-blue rounded panel holding the Latent Denoiser z_psi(z_tau, tau). A feedback loop through z_tau is marked 'x N_cont', and the noise start is z_1 ~ N(0, I). A solid blue arrow carries z into the right zone. That zone is a light-green panel holding the Decoder x_theta(x_t, z). Its own loop through x_t is marked 'x N_disc', and the start is x_1 ~ pi_mask. Output x exits at the right. At bottom left, a small inset shows a curved trajectory with red dashed shortcut lines, labelled 'Self-distillation' and u_eta. A red dash-dot arrow points from it to the latent diffusion panel. Color-coding by stage guides the eye from left to right.
caption: DiLaDiff: hybrid continuous-discrete diffusion with self-distilled latent. The latent space is crafted with encoder Eϕ and decoder xθ and learned a posteriori with a diffusion process with denoiser zψ. The latent diffusion trajectories are further self-distilled with MeanFlow student uη(zτ,τ,r).
abstract: Diffusion language models intrinsically fail to capture correlations between decoded tokens, which leads to a harsh trade-off between sampling quality and throughput. To solve this issue, we propose DiLaDiff, a variant of masked diffusion language models with three components: (1) a continuous latent space with semantic capabilities, learned by an auto-encoder fine-tuned from an existing masked diffusion language model; (2) a latent diffusion model learning the prior over the encoder distribution; (3) a consistency model distilling the learned prior into a few-step latent generative model. We show that, even without distillation, our latent-guided diffusion model outperforms the masked diffusion baseline while significantly accelerating inference. Consistency distillation further lowers the computational overhead of continuous diffusion, such that the latent is generated in negligible time compared to discrete decoding.
